findings.source_quote: καὶ ἐδίδαξεν ἕκαστος [κατὰ] τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων.
findings.english_quote: “According to” translates a bracketed insertion in the printed source, absent from Athos as reported. Desire for gain, the continuing penalty, and the stated difference between available and unavailable repentance remain explicit.
findings.issue: Note c correctly identifies the editorial insertion, but incompletely discloses the supplied apparatus report for this clause. It omits the attribution to Hilgenfeld and the reported version support, despite the source warning to retain attribution of version-supported editorial readings. It also leaves undisclosed the expressly supplied report that Latin Palatina and Ethiopic omit ἕκαστος, translated as “each.” This is a bounded note-disclosure defect, not grounds for replacing the selected working text.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise note c to identify [κατά] as Hilgenfeld’s editorial insertion, reported with support from Latin Vulgata, Latin Palatina, and Ethiopic and absent from Athos. Also state that the apparatus reports Latin Palatina and Ethiopic omitting the preceding ἕκαστος (“each”). Attribute these details to the supplied edition-apparatus transcription, without claiming fresh witness verification. Retain the selected main-text reading; any revised note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ἐδίδαξεν ἕκαστος [κατὰ] τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων.
findings.english_quote: “According to” translates a bracketed insertion in the printed source, absent from Athos as reported. Desire for gain, the continuing penalty, and the stated difference between available and unavailable repentance remain explicit.
findings.issue: Independent comparison with the Greek supports “Each taught according to the desires of people who were sinning,” including the disclosed editorial supplement. However, note c omits the supplied attribution of [κατά] to Hilgenfeld and its reported version support. It also omits the supplied report that Latin Palatina and Ethiopic lack ἕκαστος (“each”). The simplified edition therefore inherits an incomplete disclosure of the editorial basis and the reported alternative affecting its explicit “Each.”
findings.suggested_revision: Expand note c to attribute the insertion to Hilgenfeld, identify the reported support from Latin Vulgata, Latin Palatina, and Ethiopic and its reported absence from Athos, and disclose the Latin Palatina/Ethiopic omission of “each.” Present these as edition-reported readings, not independently verified manuscript readings. Do not automatically change the selected English clause; submit the revised note for fresh review.

summary: Both editions cover every selected Greek clause and preserve the severe denial of repentance, the conditional opportunity for the second group, the continuing penalty, speaker distinctions, and servant terminology. Their main texts are faithful to the disclosed working readings. Both require a limited correction to note c’s editorial attribution and reported-variant disclosure. This assessment concerns the supplied text and attributed reports, not authentication of unseen manuscripts or exhaustive collation.
